A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural-operator framework for compressed sensing MRI. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including matching content relocated in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original fastMRI knee and brain reconstruction experiments, cross-pattern and cross-rate evaluations, zero-shot reconstruction results, ablations, and inference timings.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds kernel-basis comparisons and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated kernel basis from Zernike polynomials to piecewise-linear functions. However, v3 already describes the same basis-ring configuration retained in v4 Appendix B.3. The PDFs do not resolve whether this changes the implemented method or corrects its description; the unrolled architecture and SSIM loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use fastMRI multi-coil knee and T2 brain data with the same undersampling patterns, rates, super-resolution scenarios, and extended-FOV evaluations. The new basis experiment uses a subset of the existing knee dataset.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including Zero-filled, l1-Wavelet, U-Net, E2E-VN/E2E-VN++, CSGM, ScoreMRI, and PnP-DM. The new basis study compares internal model variants, while the computational-cost table uses existing diffusion comparators.

E3.justification: The new basis experiment uses one cascade, 30% of fastMRI knee training data, 15 epochs, and kernels with similar parameter counts (Appendix B.3). Table 10 adds forward-pass and GFLOP measurements per inference. Existing reconstruction training and evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds a controlled comparison of piecewise-linear, Zernike, and Morlet bases (Table 4) and a computational-cost analysis (Table 10). Existing kernel-interpolation, equal-parameter, and NOk ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing ± reporting and plotted uncertainty bands are retained. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added; the new basis and computational-cost tables report point values.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises E2E-VN inference time from 0.06 to 0.104 seconds and NO from 0.06 to 0.158 seconds. New Table 4 reports PSNRs of 36.125, 32.983, and 32.755 for piecewise-linear, Zernike, and Morlet bases. Table 10 adds computational results, including 171 GFLOPs for NO versus 630K–950K for diffusion methods. Main reconstruction scores and matched appendix benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework, DISCO definitions, quadrature approximation, CNN pointwise-limit derivation, and Zernike completeness argument are retained. Appendix E.2 presents Zernike as an example among several kernel bases without changing the existing derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the claimed inference speedup over diffusion methods from 1,400× to 600×. The core claims of unified reconstruction across undersampling patterns and resolutions, reconstruction-quality advantages, and zero-shot capabilities remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 motivates selecting the piecewise-linear basis through its empirical comparison and explicitly attributes diffusion's large computational cost to thousands of forward passes. The limitations concerning exploration of only DISCO and the absence of diagnostic-accuracy evaluation are unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly identifies the implemented basis as piecewise linear and documents the new basis experiment. Table 3 specifies NVIDIA A100 timing hardware and changes its diffusion-tuning estimate from approximately 12 to 6 hours per pattern, matching the existing prose. The code-access information and principal implementation hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The same 44 referenced works and substantive positioning relative to CNN reconstruction, diffusion methods, and neural operators are retained. Citation-location and reference-page changes do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v4 condenses and rewrites the abstract, edits explanatory passages and captions, expands acknowledgments, and renames Appendix E.2. The overall narrative and main-section and appendix ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is restyled and uses generic CNN labels, Figure 7 is enlarged to span both columns, and Figure 12 is reformatted with clearer axis labeling. Two tables are added and appendix displays are repositioned; most existing figures and tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: v4 adds controlled evidence for kernel selection and a computational-cost breakdown, identifies timing hardware, and recalibrates its headline speed claim to the revised latency results. These improve empirical support and transparency. The main reconstruction evidence and clinical limitations remain unchanged, and whether the basis description reflects an implementation change remains unresolved, so the overall improvement is limited.
